facts.text: Bloomingdale was incorporated as a village in 1852 and quickly became a hub for the lumbering industry.
The hamlet’s location on the Saranac River and at the junction of five roads, including New York State Route 3, kept it active even as lumbering declined.
Bloomingdale’s historic brownstones and prewar apartments were restored by a new generation of residents in the 1970s, sparking a wave of community activism.
The Bloomingdale Branch of the New York Public Library opened in 1896, becoming a cornerstone of local education and community life.
In 1900, Daniel Seckington opened one of Essex County’s earliest golf courses at the Waverly House, a nine‑hole course that still echoes the town’s early leisure culture.
Bloomingdale’s riverfront remained industrial, dotted with warehouses and New York Central Railroad freight lines, while the inland streets kept a quiet residential feel.
